_about: Real answers, saved so the refusals are tested on what Jupiter says rather than what a test imagined. 'measured' ones were fetched on 5 Sep 2026 with curl against the live hosts and cost nothing; 'documented' ones are copied from Jupiter's Ultra API response reference (developers.jup.ag/docs/ultra/response).

unknownMint.source: measured, lite-api.jup.ag /ultra/v1/order for a mint that does not exist

emptyWalletOrder.source: measured, lite-api.jup.ag /ultra/v1/order to buy $10 of SOL for a wallet holding nothing, trimmed to the fields read; the requestId is a stand-in for the real one

executeGarbage.source: measured, lite-api.jup.ag /ultra/v1/execute with a transaction that is not a transaction

orderNoFunds.source: documented, /order errorCode 1; also seen live on 4 Sep 2026 as errorMessage 'Insufficient funds' on a JUP quote for the empty test wallet

executeOrderNotFound.source: documented, /execute code -1: the order went stale before it was sent

body.error: Order not found, it might have expired

executeExpired.source: documented, /execute code -1005: never reached the network

executeSlippage.source: documented, /execute code 6001: landed on the chain and failed there

executeRfqInternal.source: documented, /execute code -2005: Jupiter's own market maker fell over

executeProgramFailed.source: made up from the documented shape: a program error the app has no name for, on a transaction that landed
